items.title: Mononoke
items.reason: Across the complete 12-episode 2007 television series, the wandering Medicine Seller investigates five supernatural cases, each involving a dangerous spirit born from concealed human wrongdoing. He cannot draw his exorcism sword until he establishes the spirit's Form, Truth and Reason, making interrogations, contradictory accounts, concealed motives and successive revelations central to every arc. Hauntings at an inn, on a ship, in a prison, during an incense contest and aboard a train provide unsettling supernatural threats, psychological horror and a striking visual language of patterned paper textures, ukiyo-e-inspired imagery, theatrical staging and surreal transformations. Human cruelty, murder and tragic secrets give the investigations weight, though graphic gore is intermittent rather than a constant focus. Limitations: this is primarily an episodic detective-horror anthology, not sustained adversarial psychological chess or action-heavy fantasy. The protagonist starts highly capable; training, power progression and varied combat techniques are minimal. Whole-series reviewers disagree on the deliberately restricted animation, dense symbolism and slow, dialogue-heavy pacing; some find the formula repetitive and the final case insufficient as a larger series conclusion. Evidence is restricted to the original 2007 television series, not its Ayakashi predecessor or later films.
